evidence.observation: get_parser() builds the single configargparse.ArgumentParser that binds one option table to three input sources: explicit CLI tokens, AIDER_* environment variables (auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_"), and YAML config files (config_file_parser_class=YAMLConfigFileParser). default_config_files carries the ordered .aider.conf.yml search list computed by the caller, so this constructor is where the input-source precedence layers are declared.

Within get_parser the --set-env (append, ENV_VAR_NAME=value) and --api-key (append, PROVIDER=KEY) actions are declared at lines 96-112. They are ordinary parsed options whose accumulated values main() later writes into os.environ, making them a post-parse input source that mutates the process environment consumed by runtime LLM clients.

Within get_parser the explicit file-override inputs are declared: -c/--config with is_config_file=True (lines 789-797) forces a single named config file and bypasses default_config_files, and --env-file (lines 800-805) defaults to default_env_file(git_root) and is consumed by load_dotenv_files() in main(). Because both are normal parser actions, a CLI-supplied value outranks any config-file/env-derived value for the same key.

default_env_file(git_root) resolves the implicit .env location to git_root/.env when a git root exists, otherwise ".env" in the CWD. It is the lowest-precedence default for the --env-file key that main() feeds into load_dotenv_files().

resolve_aiderignore_path() shows the pattern for path-valued options: absolute paths pass through, relative paths are re-anchored to git_root when known. Effective option values therefore depend on the runtime-discovered repo context, not solely on the raw input token.

The args module's own entrypoint (aider --md/--dotenv/--yaml/--completion) calls get_parser([], None) and parse_known_args() to instantiate action.env_var values for help/sample generation (get_md_help/get_sample_yaml/get_sample_dotenv). It confirms --config/--env-file are ordinary parser options rendered per-source by the formatter classes.

The precedence driver: main() assembles default_config_files as [CWD/.aider.conf.yml, git_root/.aider.conf.yml, ~/.aider.conf.yml] (lines 464-477), parses once, reverses the list before rebuilding the parser (line 494) so the CWD file is loaded last and wins, then loads .env files and calls parse_args again (lines 501-504) so AIDER_* values injected from .env are picked up as an environment input source.

generate_search_path_list() produces the ordered, de-duplicated file search list used for .env, model settings and model metadata: home dir, then git root, then CWD/default, then an explicit command-line file. Duplicates are removed preserving the first resolved occurrence, so the explicit --env-file/--model-settings-file entry sits at the highest-precedence end of the list.

load_dotenv_files() consumes that ordered list, prepends ~/.aider/oauth-keys.env so it loads first and can be overridden, then calls load_dotenv(..., override=True) per file. Because override=True and files are processed in list order, later files (CWD, then explicit --env-file) overwrite earlier OS environment values for the same key.

Post-parse environment injection inside main(): --set-env entries are split into NAME=value and written to os.environ (lines 590-599); --api-key entries are uppercased to PROVIDER_API_KEY (lines 601-610); --anthropic-api-key/--openai-api-key are copied into ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY (lines 612-616); deprecated --openai-api-* flags and handle_deprecated_model_args follow (lines 619-634). This is where parsed options become runtime environment inputs for downstream LLM clients.

get_io() is the runtime consumer boundary for display/IO options: it reads fields straight off the parsed namespace (yes_always, history files, colors, code_theme, encoding, line_endings, fancy_input, multiline, notifications) and constructs InputOutput. Consumers never re-read CLI/config/env, so whichever source won at parse time is what is used here.

Derived runtime consumption inside main(): model settings files are registered (lines 756-757), model choice is finalized via select_default_model then args.model is updated (lines 777-783), map_tokens falls back to main_model.get_repo_map_tokens() when args.map_tokens is None (lines 965-968), and the whole namespace is threaded into Coder.create (lines 973-1007) with edit_format, auto_commits, dry_run, lint_cmds, map_refresh, cache_prompts, etc. This shows resolved config is consumed at object construction, after precedence is settled.

Coder.create() is the terminal runtime consumer for edit/model settings: it accepts edit_format (from args.edit_format) and falls back to main_model.edit_format when unset, constructs the coder via coder(main_model, io, **kwargs), and raises UnknownEditFormat for an unsupported format. It evidences that resolved options flow into object construction rather than being re-read.

select_default_model(args, io, analytics) shows model-selection precedence: if args.model is set (from CLI, AIDER_MODEL env var, or config file) it is returned unchanged (lines 129-130); otherwise it auto-selects a model from whichever API keys are present (line 132). Explicit --model/config/env therefore outranks key-derived defaults.

The YAML config docs state the .aider.conf.yml locations (home dir, git root, current dir) are loaded in that order and 'Files loaded last will take priority', and that --config <filename> loads only that one file. This documents the config-file half of the precedence chain implemented in aider/main.py.

The .env docs state the lookup order (home dir, git root, current dir, then --env-file) and that 'Files loaded last will take priority', matching load_dotenv_files()' override=True sequential loading.

Documents the alias precedence: command-line aliases (highest), then configuration-file aliases, then built-in aliases (lowest), matching how main() applies args.alias onto models.MODEL_ALIASES after built-ins are registered.

claims.claim: Aider resolves each option from a layered set of input sources with precedence: explicit command-line token > AIDER_* environment variable / .env entry > .aider.conf.yml config file > built-in argparse default. The sources are declared together by get_parser(), which enables CLI parsing, auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_" env binding, and YAML config-file parsing on the same parser, so a higher layer overwrites the same key from a lower layer.

The config-file tier is itself ordered: main() builds default_config_files as [CWD, git root, home], reverses it before creating the final parser, and loads files in that reversed order, so the current-directory .aider.conf.yml is applied last and wins over the git-root and home files. Passing --config (is_config_file=True) replaces the default list entirely with the single named file.

The .env tier is ordered by generate_search_path_list() and applied by load_dotenv_files(): ~/.aider/oauth-keys.env is prepended and loaded first (so it can be overridden), followed by home, git root, CWD and finally the explicit --env-file; each file is loaded with override=True, so the last-listed file wins for a duplicated key and the resulting AIDER_* values are visible to the parser on its final parse_args() pass.

Some options are not merely read but converted into runtime environment inputs after parsing: --set-env writes NAME=value into os.environ, --api-key writes <PROVIDER>_API_KEY, and --openai-api-key/--anthropic-api-key write OPENAI_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These actions live in get_parser() and the injection happens in main(), so they feed downstream consumers (litellm/model clients) rather than being used as argv/config values.

The parsed namespace is the single runtime-consumer contract: display/IO options are read directly in get_io() to build InputOutput; model choice is finalized by select_default_model() where an explicit --model/config/env value short-circuits key-derived auto-selection; and coder/behavior options are threaded into Coder.create(). No consumer re-reads the CLI/config/env layers, so the precedence resolved during startup is what the runtime actually executes.

Alias resolution is another explicit precedence table: command-line --alias definitions override configuration-file aliases, which override built-in aliases, matching main() writing args.alias entries onto models.MODEL_ALIASES after the built-ins exist.

conclusion: Aider funnels every option through a single configargparse parser created by aider/args.py:get_parser(). The input-source precedence is: (1) explicit CLI token, (2) AIDER_* environment variable (including values injected from .env), (3) .aider.conf.yml config file, (4) built-in argparse default. Within the config-file tier, main() orders default files [CWD, git root, home], reverses them so the CWD file loads last and wins, and --config replaces that default set with one file. Within the .env tier, load_dotenv_files() loads oauth-keys.env first then home/git-root/CWD/--env-file with override=True, so the most specific file wins and the injected AIDER_* keys are then re-parsed. After parsing, main() converts --set-env/--api-key/--*-api-key into os.environ for runtime LLM clients, applies derived defaults (dark/light mode colors, map_tokens, map_refresh), and hands the namespace to the runtime consumers get_io()/InputOutput, select_default_model(), and Coder.create() — none of which re-reads the lower layers.
